newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, but seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, but seen rebounding.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.26 percent on Thursday, but traders said they expected the market to trade with a firmer bias due to renewed optimism.
"The good performance of last week's listing of Lek's A issue brought optimism to the market and could fuel growth over the next week," one trader said.
Since being listed on Wednesday last week, Lek's A shares have risen 18.1 percent.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 2.46 points to 928.72.
* Nine shares fell and three rose, while 12 were untraded.
* Turnover eased to 127.7 million tolars from 168.2 million.
* Drug company's Lek A issue had the highest turnover and was the top gainer, rising 2.86 percent to 16,265 tolars on volume of 5,407 shares for total turnover of 87.9 million tolars.
* Bank UBK was the leading decliner, falling five percent to 8,550 on volume of two shares for total turnover of 0.02 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
